opti-1: High in the mountains, every park holds a mystery.
opti-2: In 1988, giant fires burn across Yellowstone.
opti-3: When the smoke clears, black trunks stand everywhere.
opti-4: But look closer. Tiny pine trees are growing back.
opti-5: Scientists count them, one small square at a time.
opti-6: On beaches, scientists watch which way the hatchlings go.
opti-7: Ask. Predict. Collect evidence. You've done it all year.
opti-8: What have you learned to do as a scientist this year, and how can you prove it?
33-02-welcome: It's our season finale! First, inspect two old pages from a real scientist's field book.
33-02-lesson: Three scenarios, three investigations: a burned forest, a bright beach, and a mountain that's getting warmer.
33-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
33-02-assign: Your last assignment of the year! Show your evidence, draw your year, then premiere your film.
how-33-02-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the page, then tap three things you notice.
how-33-02-compare: Put the hatchling under one beach and the low lights under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a beach. Press Let the hatchlings go. Then swap.
how-33-02-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing stop: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-33-02-det: Pick three cards, one at a time. Tap something you see, then name the science topic. Predict what scientists figured out, and see the evidence.
how-33-02-partc: Make your My Year as a Scientist page. Draw a model of your scenario with at least three labels and arrows that show cause and effect.
